chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Make for me white caps and do not break them, for the Master like me does not wear the broken one'.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the condition of the caps he wore?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies the production of white, intact caps (*qalanis*), linking the physical wholeness of the garment to the dignity (*mawqif*) of the Imam. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *adab* (etiquette) and the symbolic purity associated with white attire, distinguishing the Imam's status as a 'master' who wears what is unblemished, both literally and spiritually. The instruction underscores the importance of preserving the integrity of the Imam's personal effects as a sign of respect and continuity in his lineage.
